---
title: "Learning Statistics with an App"
params:
  lang: "en"
---

```{r, include=FALSE}
library(exams)
library(mathml)
library(htmltools)
library(mistakes)

task <- "tgroups7"
plfile <- sprintf("%s.pl", task)
if(!file.exists(plfile))
  plfile <- system.file(file.path("rexams", plfile), package = "mistakes")
rolog::consult(plfile)

hook(m_A, mean("A"))
hook(s_A, subscript(s, "A"))
hook(n_A, subscript(N, "A"))
hook(m_B, mean("B"))
hook(s_B, subscript(s, "B"))
hook(n_B, subscript(N, "B"))
hook(s_pool, subscript(s, "pool"))

repeat
{
  # unequal group sizes, so that the weighting of the variances matters
  n_A <- sample(15:40, 1)
  n_B <- sample(15:40, 1)
  if(n_A == n_B)
    next

  s_A <- round(runif(1, 5, 10), 1)
  s_B <- round(s_A * runif(1, 0.6, 1.4), 1)
  m_B <- round(runif(1, 25, 35), 1)

  t <- runif(1, 0.5, 3.0)
  v_pool <- ((n_A - 1) * s_A^2 + (n_B - 1) * s_B^2) / (n_A + n_B - 2)
  m_A <- round(m_B + t * sqrt(v_pool * (1/n_A + 1/n_B)), 1)
  tratio <- (m_A - m_B) / sqrt(v_pool * (1/n_A + 1/n_B))

  if(tratio < 0.5 || tratio > 3.0)
    next

  Q <- substitute(search(task, tgroups(m_A, s_A, n_A, m_B, s_B, n_B),
                    .S, .R, .P, .E), list(task = as.name(task)))
  S <- findall(Q, options=list(preproc=as.rolog), env=environment())

  if(problems(S))
    next

  # response options must be distinguishable after rounding
  if(any(duplicated(sprintf("%.2f", sapply(S, FUN="[[", "R")))))
    next

  break
}

tab <- data.frame(A = c(sprintf("%.1f", c(m_A, s_A)), n_A),
                  B = c(sprintf("%.1f", c(m_B, s_B)), n_B))
row.names(tab) <- c("Mean", "SD", "N")

t <- prepare(task=task, S)
sol <- format_feedback(t$correct, t$explanations, t$bugs, t$praise, t$blame, t$extra)
sol <- lapply(sol, FUN=gsub, pattern="\\n", replacement="")
```

Question
========
A study investigates whether students who prepare for a statistics exam with a 
learning app (Group A) achieve better results than students who prepare with a 
textbook (Group B). A total of $N_A=`r n_A`$ students learn with the app, and 
$N_B=`r n_B`$ students learn with the textbook. The outcome is the number of points 
in the final exam (from 0 to 60 points). The variances in both groups are assumed to be equal.
The significance level is set to $\alpha=.05$, two-tailed.

````{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(tab, align="r", caption="_Table 1._ Exam points in Group A (app) and Group B (textbook).")
````
Do the two groups differ in their exam results? 
Please report the $t$-ratio.

```{r questionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(t$alternatives, markup="markdown")
```

Solution
========
The $t$-statistic for independent samples is given by 
$t=\frac{\overline{A}-\overline{B}}{\sqrt{s_\text{pool}^2 \left(\frac{1}{N_A}+\frac{1}{N_B}\right)}}$
with the pooled variance $s_\text{pool}^2=\frac{(N_A-1)\, s_A^2 + (N_B-1)\, s_B^2}{N_A+N_B-2}$, 
resulting in `r t$solution`

```{r solutionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(sol, markup="markdown")
```
